clue.text: A great many put heart into craft

indicators.note: with 'put' before it, this says one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: SS stands for steamship, a craft
the core of something is its heart

explanation.surface: Someone puts a great deal of feeling into their handiwork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'craft' looks like skill, but here it is a vessel; 'put' and 'into' together signal the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Scores of things means a large number of them, a score being twenty.

clue.text: Member taken in by one learning to appeal

indicators.note: the member is absorbed within the letters for the other two pieces

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
lore is traditional knowledge or learning
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A politician is coached by a scholar on how to make an appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: To implore is to beg, the same as to make an earnest appeal.

clue.text: Scientific device to swindle the less astute

parts.note: a con is a swindle
denser means more stupid, so less astute

explanation.surface: A gadget sold to fleece gullible buyers.
explanation.definitionFit: A condenser is a piece of laboratory or electrical apparatus.

clue.text: Concerned with some cattle show

parts.note: re means regarding or concerning
veal is meat from calves, a kind of cattle

explanation.surface: Someone keen on a livestock exhibition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'show' looks like a noun completing 'cattle show', but it is the verb definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To reveal something is to show or disclose it.

clue.text: Make much of the small firm's place

parts.note: Co is the short form of company, so the firm's is Co's
to set something is to place it

explanation.surface: Praising the premises of a little company.
explanation.definitionFit: To cosset is to pamper, to make a great fuss of someone.

clue.text: Stupidly calls it a part of Spain in Spanish

indicators.note: doing something stupidly signals these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone foolishly names a region of Spain in the wrong way.
explanation.definitionFit: Castilla is the native Spanish name for the region English calls Castile.

clue.text: Guide young ox

explanation.definitionFit: Both a verb of direction and a word for a young bullock raised for beef.

clue.text: No longer working? That's tough!

parts.note: ex means former, no longer so
acting means serving or functioning, so working

explanation.surface: A retired person remarks that retirement is hard going.
explanation.definitionFit: An exacting task is demanding, hard to satisfy.

clue.text: Gets settled and makes up

definitions.meaning: to compose a poem or tune is to create it

explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers calming oneself and also creating music or writing.

clue.text: Fool Oriental soldier about a weapon

parts.note: an ass is a fool
E stands for East, the Orient

indicators.note: the soldier's letters go around the next piece

parts.note: GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: An Eastern soldier, a fool, is caught carrying a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: An assegai is a light spear used in southern Africa.

clue.text: Lined as ordered

explanation.definitionFit: Paper marked with straight lines, and also governed or commanded.

clue.text: Judge in need of new bar attire

indicators.note: a new version of the letters is a rearrangement of them

explanation.surface: A barrister needs fresh courtroom robes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar attire' pictures a lawyer's gown, but it is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To arbitrate is to settle a dispute as an impartial referee.

clue.text: Backed by a salesman

indicators.note: something backed is turned around, read from the end

parts.note: per means by or for each, as in per annum

explanation.surface: Someone is supported by a sales agent.
explanation.definitionFit: A rep is a sales representative.

clue.text: The Left is beset by unwonted squeeze

indicators.note: being beset means surrounded, so one piece lies within the other

parts.note: unwonted means unusual, so strange

explanation.surface: A political left wing is besieged by an unusual crunch.
explanation.definitionFit: To strangle is to squeeze the throat.

clue.text: Hidden talent re-discovered

indicators.note: found again in a new form, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: An unseen gift comes to light once more.
explanation.definitionFit: Latent means present but dormant or concealed.

clue.text: A large number charge for entrance

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500
a mission is a task one is charged with

explanation.surface: A big fee demanded for getting in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charge' looks like a price, but it is a duty given to someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Admission is the act or right of entering a place.

clue.text: Barely-used pied-a terre in ancient city?

definitions.text: Barely-used pied-a terre in ancient city?

parts.words: Barely-used pied-a terre in ancient city?
parts.note: a room in the Roman spa city of Bath, and also a room used while bare, when washing

explanation.surface: A rarely visited flat kept in an old town.
explanation.walkthrough: Bath is an English city famed for its Roman baths; 'Barely-used' means used by the bare, not seldom used.
explanation.definitionFit: A room for washing in is one where people are naked, and also reads as a room in Bath.

clue.text: In brief, this creature's an amphibian

definitions.text: In brief, this creature's an amphibian

parts.words: In brief, this creature's an amphibian
parts.note: a short word, in brief, for a small salamander-like animal

explanation.surface: A short remark that a certain animal lives on land and in water.
explanation.definitionFit: An eft is a young newt, a small amphibian, and the word is very brief.

clue.text: Many fewer accept a note without qualms

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: far less means many fewer
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: Far fewer people take on a musical note.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone fearless acts boldly, free of hesitation or anxiety.

clue.text: Putrid fish is sent back

indicators.note: something sent back is returned, so it is read the other way

parts.note: a dab is a small flatfish

explanation.surface: A rotten fish is returned to the shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Bad food is rotten or spoilt.

clue.text: A Gallic writer's wrongful arrest

indicators.note: wrongful suggests the letters are set out in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A French author is wrongly detained.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean-Paul Sartre was a French philosopher, novelist and playwright.

clue.text: Club formed by some probationers

indicators.note: only some of the word's letters are used, a run from inside it

explanation.surface: A society set up by offenders on probation.
explanation.definitionFit: A bat is a club used in cricket or baseball.

clue.text: The top man who is popular

explanation.definitionFit: A high-ranking officer, and something common to most of the public.

clue.text: Crash involving state in a manner of speaking

indicators.note: to involve is to include, so one piece contains the other

parts.note: an accent is a way of pronouncing words
ID is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Idaho

explanation.surface: A collision that tangles up a nation's way of talking.
explanation.definitionFit: An accident is an unplanned mishap such as a collision.

clue.text: With the cold a seed's development stopped

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

indicators.note: development changes the shape of the letters, rearranging them

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: Cold weather halted a seed's growth.
explanation.definitionFit: Ceased means came to an end, halted.

clue.text: Row about batting less

indicators.note: one piece goes around the other

parts.note: a tier is a row of seats
in cricket, the side batting is in

explanation.surface: An argument breaks out over a poorer batting performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like a quarrel but is a line of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinier means smaller, littler in size.

clue.text: That 27 could well be indifferent!

indicators.note: the letters could be turned into something else, a sign of rearrangement

parts.note: the answer to clue 27, a word for a horseman

explanation.surface: Someone suggests a certain horseman may be mediocre.
explanation.definitionFit: Third-rate means poor quality, and indifferent can mean mediocre.

clue.text: He's up-comment's called for!

definitions.meaning: a horseman is up in the saddle
an additional clause or remark added to a statement or verdict

explanation.definitionFit: Someone mounted on a horse, and also an added note to a document.

clue.text: Polish man held by Oriental coppers

parts.note: sen are small coins of Japan and other Eastern countries
he is a male pronoun, standing for a man

explanation.surface: A Polish man is detained by Asian police officers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' looks like a nationality but is the noun for a gloss; 'coppers' are coins, not police.
explanation.definitionFit: Polish and sheen both mean a glossy shine.

clue.text: Sleeping accommodation on the way?

parts.note: a bed placed on a road, read literally, rather than a traveller's lodging

explanation.surface: Somewhere to stay overnight on a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadbed is the foundation layer on which a road or railway is laid.

clue.text: The last month to speak out for honour

parts.note: Dec is short for December, the last month
to orate is to make a speech

explanation.surface: In December someone speaks up for their honour.
explanation.definitionFit: To decorate someone is to honour them with a medal.

clue.text: A good man strikes back — suffers for it

indicators.note: read back to front, so the letters run in reverse

parts.note: St, saint, is a good man
rams means strikes hard

explanation.surface: A good person hits back and pays the price.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns both pieces round together, not just the strikes; 'for it' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: To smart is to sting or feel pain.
